# Embedded tracing measurement, October 20, 2026

All 20 original cells passed their workload, resource, exit and official
Collector drain gates. **None of the four CPU budgets qualifies.** These results
do not qualify a release or maximum service capacity. The failed October 17
study remains unchanged in [its original report](RESULTS-2026-10-17.md).

## Fixed method

The [method was declared before admission](https://github.com/durable-workflow/workflow/issues/773#issuecomment-6294532491).
Candidate `b2d394c5c3e16484c798f3e7a7293bfb001b07eb`, tree
`37651d791f918a80fab9d19cc31d408a9504599e`, was compared with normally installed
published Core **2.7.3**, `dda951d93f58b82447348f1b3b4e4e17dba149fb`.
All other Composer package references matched. No later diagnostic correction
was inserted into this source or measurement.

The isolated amd64 host had eight logical AMD EPYC-Genoa CPUs, approximately
16 GiB RAM, Microsoft virtualization, Linux 6.8.0-146, cgroup v2 and no swap.
Docker was 29.1.3, Compose 2.40.3, PHP 8.3.35 with CLI OPcache disabled,
Laravel 13.37, OpenTelemetry API 1.10.1, SDK 1.15.0 and OTLP exporter 1.4.0.
Builds and installation completed before admission. No unrelated application
workload or build was run during the study. Bounded administrative SSH reads
continued. The host and all experiment state were retired after results.

The accepting official Collector was
`otel/opentelemetry-collector:0.163.1@sha256:f0e23036dce3db3f9cb80d907c75a0d034cd32e93511a1943482d46129b9ae9c`.
The application used the existing four-span queue, two-span batch and 100 ms
transport timeout; Collector counters independently matched ended spans after
complete provider drain. Export failure observations did not change, and
refused/receiver-failed counters remained zero. No span payloads were retained.

Each cell used a fresh database/application, four workers and identical caps:
HTTP application 0.5 CPU / 512 MiB; each worker 1 CPU / 384 MiB; MySQL 1 CPU /
2 GiB; Redis 0.1 CPU / 128 MiB; Collector and probe each 0.2 CPU / 256 MiB.
The primary quantity sums exact cgroup CPU deltas for these nine containers
through business completion and export drain. Setup, warmup, audit queries,
sampling tools and teardown are outside those deltas. The one-second requested
sampling interval was approximately 1.26 seconds in practice; exact CPU counters
do not depend on that interval. Memory observations are sampled, not allocation
or simultaneous-peak measurements.

Ordinary cells offered one one-activity workflow per second for 120 seconds
(120 measured completions), following 30 warmups. Fan-out cells offered one
64-activity workflow per minute for 120 seconds (two measured completions),
following one warmup. Original observer/run/execution bounds remained
90/100/120 seconds. Repetitions rotated base/off/on, on/base/off, off/on/base,
then repeated the baseline for drift, separately for each workload. No extra
repetition was selected after results.

## CPU acceptance

Estimates use the mean of three paired candidate/baseline ratios, two-sided
95% paired-t intervals, n=3, df=2. Both the upper endpoint and absolute final
baseline drift must fit the declared budget. Negative estimates do not prove
an improvement. The budgets remain unchanged for this study.

| Workload | Profile | Mean | 95% interval | Baseline drift | Budget | Qualified |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Ordinary | Disabled | +1.11% | [-7.40%, +9.62%] | +1.62% | 1% | No |
| Ordinary | Enabled | +9.46% | [+1.35%, +17.56%] | +1.62% | 5% | No |
| 64-member fan-out | Disabled | -0.59% | [-13.91%, +12.72%] | +2.04% | 1% | No |
| 64-member fan-out | Enabled | +3.18% | [-7.85%, +14.21%] | +2.04% | 5% | No |

| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

## Other observations

All offered workflows were accepted and completed. The independent reader
validated exact callback/history counts and results, no missed offers, extra
attempts, unfinished work, failed jobs or residual queue entries. No container
OOM/restart or nonzero worker child exit occurred. MySQL, Redis and the official
Collector exited zero; HTTP and retaining shells used their declared 143 stop.
Repairs remained observable and were not substituted for extra attempts.

| Workload/profile | Observed p95 range | Observed p99 range | Sum of sampled container peaks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary/base | 1.131–1.371 s | 1.386–1.655 s | 919,670,784–924,098,560 bytes |
| Ordinary/off | 1.134–1.379 s | 1.374–1.401 s | 922,849,280–924,983,296 bytes |
| Ordinary/on | 1.388–1.393 s | 1.399–1.458 s | 944,701,440–949,186,560 bytes |
| Fan-out/base | 28.756–29.613 s | 28.756–29.613 s | 964,190,208–969,908,224 bytes |
| Fan-out/off | 28.866–29.791 s | 28.866–29.791 s | 963,702,784–971,960,320 bytes |
| Fan-out/on | 28.771–31.492 s | 28.771–31.492 s | 982,581,248–988,864,512 bytes |

Fan-out tails have only two measured observations per cell. These ranges are
descriptive, without a throughput or latency regression claim. Maximum offer
lag across cells was 74.66 ms, below the original 100 ms admission gate.

Disabled and baseline cells persisted zero tracing bytes and ended/exported
zero spans. Enabled ordinary cells, including warmup, each persisted 21,750 run
bytes and 143,400 task bytes and ended/accepted/exported exactly 1,050 spans.
Enabled fan-out cells persisted 435 run bytes and 102,813–102,814 task bytes;
their ended/accepted/exported counts were respectively 413, 403 and 401.
No activity-execution carrier bytes were stored. Different task processing and
repair observations account for differing physical span counts; the reader
verified business cardinality separately.

The prerequisites also passed: functional baseline/off/on (two runs, 65
activities each) and the published-baseline offered-load check (120 ordinary
plus two fan-out workflows). These are workload checks, not maximum-capacity
estimates. The next qualification must name its exact changed source and
published baseline, declare its method and budgets before admission, and retain
these original failures. Changing a target cannot turn this study into a pass.
